prediction.likelyOutcome: Universal's unlawful detainer claim is genuinely at risk: the three-day notice's reliance on a payment-application clause to revive a two-year-old shortfall, combined with the notice's failure to specify the rental period and 23 months of full payment acceptance in between, gives the self-represented tenant a real shot at invalidating the notice and defeating the action outright. If the notice survives, Universal likely recovers the $65,989 plus accruing holdover damages at $1,219/day, but attorney's fees cannot be quantified on this record.

Waiver/Estoppel From 23 Months of Accepted Payments

outcome.description: After a three-day court trial the trial court entered judgment for the landlord on July 3, 2025 awarding possession, $65,989 in past-due rent (the amount demanded in the notice) and $123,111 in holdover damages, $189,100 in total; no fee award is stated in the opinion. The Court of Appeal reversed, holding the three-day notice void because the unpaid rent fell due more than one year before service, and remanded for entry of judgment in favor of the tenant.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: the three-day notice was void, so the landlord takes nothing in this action.
